# Getting listed on decomp.dev

[decomp.dev](https://decomp.dev) shows progress for decompilation projects. It
reads **objdiff progress reports** (`report.json`, produced by
`objdiff-cli report generate`) that a project's GitHub Actions workflow uploads
as an artifact, and it is connected to projects through its GitHub
integration. Listed PS2 projects (for example
[OpenRAC/rac3-uya-decomp](https://github.com/OpenRAC/rac3-uya-decomp)) follow
this pattern.

## What this project already has

* `objdiff.json` generated by `configure.py` (units, progress category `main`).
* `ninja report` → `build/report.json` via `objdiff-cli report generate`.
* A byte-identical build check (`ninja` fails unless the SHA-256 matches).

## Steps

1. **Public repository** — done: this repository was split out of the private
   port project with a fresh history containing only the decomp sources.
2. **Report upload without the game in CI** — done. The retail executable is
   never uploaded anywhere, so CI does not build. After a verified local build:
   ```
   ninja                          # must print OK (byte-identical)
   ninja report
   python tools/publish_report.py # copies build/report.json to progress/report.json
   ```
   Commit `progress/report.json`; the workflow
   [`.github/workflows/report.yml`](.github/workflows/report.yml) uploads it on
   every push to `main` as the artifact **`SCUS_972.64_report`**.
   (Alternative later: a self-hosted runner that keeps the executable in a
   private folder and builds on every push; template in
   [`ci/build-and-report.yml.example`](ci/build-and-report.yml.example). On a
   public repository it must never run for pull requests from forks.)
3. **Default branch** is `main`.
4. **Register the project with decomp.dev.** A repository admin signs in at
   decomp.dev with GitHub and adds it at https://decomp.dev/manage/new (see
   https://decomp.wiki/tools/decomp-dev). Installing the decomp.dev GitHub
   app is optional (faster updates, PR comments). Provide:
   repository URL, platform PS2, game title and version (NTSC-U,
   `SCUS_972.64`) and the report artifact name. Progress appears after the
   first successful workflow run on the default branch.
5. Expected by visitors: build instructions (README.md), a license for the
   hand-written code, and progress categories (game vs. SDK) once
   translation units are identified.

## Report contents

`report.json` counts code bytes and functions per unit. In this project:

* C units: target = retail code for that address range, base = compiled C;
  functions that are byte-identical count as matched.
* Asm units: target only; their functions count towards the total but not
  towards matched code.
* Data is not tracked yet (all data stays in one asm data file).

Local check before pushing:

```
python configure.py
ninja report
```
